body.statement:
Uniformly over fixed \(S\) and all positive sample sizes, let
\[
C_{\lambda,d}:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
+\frac{d}{2\lambda+d}(\log 2)^{-2\lambda/d}.
\]
Then
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq C_{\lambda,d}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
\qquad
R_{\star,\beta}
\asymp_{\lambda,d}
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Writing
\[
a:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d},
\]
for every integer \(T\geq 3\) one has the sharper exact relations
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
\qquad
R_{\star,\beta}
=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Consequently, in any experiment for which \(R_{\star,\beta}\) is established as the sharp risk, the oracle region is
\[
N^{-\kappa}=o\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
\]
the generated-center region is
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}=o(N^{-\kappa}),
\]
and the boundary is
\[
N\asymp
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr)^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
Under independent design, or under a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition that delivers \(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2\lambda/d}\), one instead has the exact relations
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}},
\qquad
R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}\) removes a classical measurement-error inverse problem from the historical design; accordingly the defined bookkeeping contains neither a deconvolution term nor a separate moving-Gram rate. Finally, \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}\) whenever \(\lambda>1\). These algebraic conclusions do not by themselves assert that either frontier is sharp for a statistical experiment.
body.justification: The exact diagram distinguishes a genuinely active information channel from a bookkeeping term and records higher-order saturation.
body.gap: The repeated-measurement literature has a sparse-to-dense smoothing transition, while generated-regressor and measurement-error papers imply different first-stage effects; no existing result locates this oracle boundary.
body.consumer: A study can allocate its data budget to the active axis and avoid unnecessary deconvolution when the historical paths are exact.
body.proof_tex:
Put
\[
a:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}\in(0,1),
\qquad
q:=\frac{2\lambda}{d}>0.
\]
The displayed ranges follow from \(\lambda>0\) and \(d>0\). We first establish the scalar inequality used below. For \(u>0\), define
\[
\phi(u):=au+(1-a)-u^a.
\]
Then \(\phi(1)=0\) and
\[
\phi'(u)=a\bigl(1-u^{a-1}\bigr).
\]
Because \(a-1<0\), the derivative is negative for \(0<u<1\) and positive for \(u>1\). Hence \(u=1\) minimizes \(\phi\), and therefore
\[
x^a y^{1-a}\leq ax+(1-a)y,
\qquad x>0,\quad y>0,
\]
after substituting \(u=x/y\) and multiplying by \(y\).

The definitions of \(a\) and \(q\) give
\[
q(1-a)
=\frac{2\lambda}{d}\frac{d}{2\lambda+d}
=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
=a.
\]
For each cohort \(s\), the positivity of \(T\) and \(n_s\) permits the preceding inequality with \(x=n_s^{-1}\) and \(y=T^{-q}\). Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
&=n_s^{-a}T^{-a}\\
&=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-q})^{1-a}\\
&\leq a n_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since the cohort weights are positive and satisfy \(\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s=1\),
\[
\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s^2
\leq \left(\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s\right)^2
=1.
\]
Multiplication of the cohortwise bound by \(\pi_s^2\), followed by summation and the definitions in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\), therefore yields
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\]

For every positive integer \(T\), one has \(\log(T\vee2)\geq\log2>0\). Consequently,
\[
T^{-q}
\leq(\log2)^{-q}
\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{q}
=(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\]
It follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
&\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\\
&\leq\bigl\{a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\bigr\}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr)\\
&=C_{\lambda,d}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, \(0<\log2<1\) and \(q>0\), so \(C_{\lambda,d}\geq a+(1-a)=1\). Define
\[
A:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
\qquad
D_0:=A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
All rate components are positive. The definition of \(R_{\star,\beta}\), the preceding upper bound, and \(C_{\lambda,d}\geq1\) imply
\[
D_0
\leq R_{\star,\beta}
=A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq D_0\vee(C_{\lambda,d}A)
\leq C_{\lambda,d}D_0.
\]
Thus
\[
R_{\star,\beta}
\asymp_{\lambda,d}
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}},
\]
with comparison constants \(1\) and \(C_{\lambda,d}\), independent of \(N\), \(T\), \(S\), and the positive replication counts.

Now suppose that \(T\geq3\). Then \(T\vee2=T\) and \(\log T\geq1\), whence
\[
T^{-q}
\leq \left(\frac{\log T}{T}\right)^q
=R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\]
Substitution into the earlier cohort-summed inequality gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
\]
where the last inequality holds because \(a\in(0,1)\). Taking the maximum with the remaining rate components in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) now gives the exact identity
\[
R_{\star,\beta}
=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]

By \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\), \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}\). Along any joint growth array, this channel is negligible relative to \(A\) exactly when \(N^{-\kappa}=o(A)\), and it dominates \(A\) exactly when \(A=o(N^{-\kappa})\). Since \(\kappa>0\), the boundary comparison \(N^{-\kappa}\asymp A\) is equivalent to
\[
N\asymp A^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
These are minimax phases only when a separate statistical theorem establishes \(R_{\star,\beta}\) as the sharp risk; the present deductions are algebraic.

For the independent-design comparator, or under a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition that delivers \(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-q}\), the cohort-summed inequality instead gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp}}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}.
\]
The comparator definition of \(R_\star\) in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) therefore implies
\[
R_\star
=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}
=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]

Assumption \(\texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}\) states that \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\). Hence evaluation of a historical-design functional at \(X_{st}\) uses the recorded coordinate itself and requires no inversion of a measurement-error convolution. Inspection of the exhaustive rate definition in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) shows that it contains neither a deconvolution component nor a separate moving-Gram component. Finally, \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\); if \(\lambda>1\), then \(\kappa=1\), and therefore
\[
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}=N^{-1}.
\]
This proves all asserted relations.
